title: Staggered pin rollout experiment notes and operator run-log
content:
Context:
We ran a controlled experiment (staggered pin rollout) to test gradual enforcement of region pins for existing tenants. Goal was to validate operator workflows, measure false-positive eviction rates, and quantify customer impact when soft-pinning transitions to hard enforcement.

Goals: 
- Validate incremental enforcement approach: soft pin (warnings + metrics) -> enforced routing -> eviction throttles.
- Measure mismatch rate where routing telemetry differs from tenant expectation (tenant thinks pinned to eu-west-1 but requests observed in us-east-1).
- Confirm rollback window and automation behave as expected for multi-tenant edge cases.

Scope and constraints: 
- 120 tenants selected (mix of enterprise + mid-market), chosen for existing mixed-region traffic and active support agreements.
- No changes to billing or legal agreements during the trial.
- Experiment excludes tenants with active private deployments on customer-managed infra.

Phases (summary):
1) Baseline collection (2 weeks): gather prefix/caching/KV access patterns, session affinity rates, and regional request distribution.
2) Soft pinging (1 week): mark tenants as pinned in metadata only; do NOT change routing. Emit warnings and capture mismatch telemetry.
3) Partial enforcement (canary, 3 days): route 20% of new sessions using pin policy (region-aware). Monitor latency, model variant fallsbacks, and cross-region cache misses.
4) Full enforcement (72h window): switch routing layer to honor pins for new sessions; existing sessions drained. Monitor operator metrics and customer-impact signals closely.

Operator run-log highlights (selected):
- 2024-11-15 09:12 UTC: initial baseline collection query run. SQL used: SELECT tenant_id, region, count(*) AS requests FROM request_log WHERE ts BETWEEN '2024-10-31' AND '2024-11-14' GROUP BY tenant_id, region ORDER BY tenant_id; (stored in JIRA-PIN-1189 comment).
- 2024-11-22 18:05 UTC: soft-pinning toggle shipped to staging. Flag: feature.pin.soft_mode=true. Observed: 14/120 tenants emitted pin-mismatch warnings within 6 hours (mostly mobile SDK clients).
- 2024-11-26 02:20 UTC: canary enforcement started for 24 tenants (evening window; low traffic). A/B traffic shadowing enabled. Two tenants (T-47, T-82) reported 5–7% error spike related to malformed X-Region headers.
- 2024-11-28 15:40 UTC: partial enforcement rollout paused for T-82 after ops detected degraded authentication token validation when routed through eu-west-1 NAT gateway. Rollback for T-82 completed by 16:05 UTC. Root cause tracked to firewall rule mismatch on the transit path (see linked GitHub PR-56).

Telemetry and queries to keep handy:
- Pin mismatch rate: curl -s 'https://telemetry.internal/api/query' -d '{"q":"pin_mismatch_rate{env="prod"}"}' | jq .
- Cross-region KV miss rate per tenant: SELECT tenant_id, region, sum(kv_misses) FROM kv_metrics WHERE window='1h' GROUP BY tenant_id, region;
- Eviction risk signal (operators): top_k(20, tenants, score=region_drift * request_volume) exported to ops dashboard.

Observed metrics (high level):
- Average latency: +18ms for pinned requests in enforced region (expected due to cache warmth).
- Tokenization throughput: unchanged.
- Cross-region cache miss delta: +11% during first 24h of enforcement, decreasing to +3% after prefix warming / prefetch queues.
- False eviction triggers: 6 incidents across 120 tenants (5% of tenants) during canary window; 4 of those tied to client-side regional hints (SDK fallback to system locale).

Operator checklist for future rollouts (working draft):
- Preflight: verify tenant metadata (region pin present and validated), confirm contact cadence with customer success.
- Staging burn: replicate tenant routing delta in staging with a copy of request sampling for 48h.
- Network checks: validate NAT/gateway rules for the target region; run connectivity smoke tests to tenant-auth endpoints.
- Telemetry knobs: enable pin_mismatch_alert=(threshold=0.5%) and kv_prefetch=(on) for 24h post-enforcement.
- Rollback plan: immediate soft-toggle revert + traffic drain timeline (30min sustained error threshold or 20% latency P99 increase).

Customer communication playbook (notes):
- For tenants in the experiment, we used the "pin-preflight" email template 48h before enforcement and a short post-enforcement summary describing expected transient cache warm-ups.
- Escalation: if customers see user-facing errors, trigger SE on-call and route to regional infra owner.

Action items and mitigations captured: 
- Improve client SDK regional hints: add a deprecation warning for locale-based region hints; prefer server-side tile. Owner: Marcus Rivera. ETA: 2025-02-10.
- Automate NAT/gateway linting in our staging infra to catch firewall misconfigs before canary. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2024-12-20.
- Add a pre-warm job: when pin transitions to enforcement, prefetch model KV prefixes for top-100 heavy tenants to reduce cache miss spike. Owner: Sam Cohen. ETA: 2025-01-05.

Unresolved questions / risks: 
- Long-lived sessions: how to reconcile session stickiness when enforcement changes mid-session? Current behaviour drains sessions but some clients reattach and pick the wrong region. Need design decision: allow session transfer or force client reauth.
- Regulatory evidence package: can we produce per-tenant signed audit of region-for-each-request after enforcement? Engineering input required for proof-of-custody packaging.

Appendix: sample operator commands and tips
- Toggle soft pin for tenant: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://controlplane.internal/tenants/T-47/pinning -d '{"mode":"soft"}'
- Promote to enforcement (new sessions only): PATCH https://controlplane.internal/tenants/T-47/pinning -d '{"mode":"enforce","apply_to":"new_sessions"}'
- Drain sessions: POST https://controlplane.internal/tenants/T-47/sessions/drain -d '{"grace_period_s":1800}'

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch for mobile SDK churn — many mismatches traced back to older SDKs that set region from device locale. We should add telemetry version-tagging per request.
- Consider a rolling prefetcher that learns top prefixes per tenant and preloads into the target region before traffic switchover.

Summary / recommendation:
Staggered enforcement works as a low-customer-impact path to stricter residency compliance if paired with aggressive pre-warming and tighter networking validation. Next rollout should expand slowly (25% tenant cohort increments), improve SDK telemetry, and automate NAT verification to reduce operator manual steps.

End of doc.
